sentiment.rationale: The company reported a solid Q4 with positive comps and EPS growth, but the forward guidance for FY2026 is cautious and essentially flat relative to the prior year's performance. Management explicitly states the outlook 'remains cautious given the persistent volatility in housing macro' and forecasts the home improvement market to be 'roughly flat this year in a range of down 1% to up 1%'. The guidance range for comparable sales (flat to up 2%) and adjusted EPS ($12.25-$12.75) does not represent a material raise from the prior year's $12.28 adjusted EPS, and management highlights multiple headwinds including tariffs, elevated mortgage rates, and cautious consumer spending. The score is slightly negative because the forward outlook is hedged and cautious despite a decent backward-looking quarter.

summary.revenue: Q4 sales were $20.6 billion, comparable sales increased 1.3%. FY2025 sales were $86.3 billion, positive comparable sales of 0.2%.
summary.eps: Q4 GAAP diluted EPS of $1.78; adjusted diluted EPS of $1.98. FY2025 adjusted EPS of $12.28, a 2% increase over last year.
summary.guidance: FY2026 sales range $92 billion to $94 billion, comparable sales flat to up 2%. Adjusted diluted EPS approximately $12.25 to $12.75. Operating margin 11.2% to 11.4%, adjusted operating margin 11.6% to 11.8%.
summary.margin: Q4 adjusted gross margin 32.7%, down 18 bps. Adjusted operating margin 9%, down 41 bps. FY2025 adjusted operating margin 12.1%, flat to prior year excluding acquisitions.
key_risks: Persistent volatility in housing macro and elevated mortgage rates creating a lock-in effect.
Consumer reluctance to make significant big-ticket discretionary DIY investments.
Unpredictable tariffs and fluid tariff policy.
Uncertainty around how much tax refunds will be spent on home improvement.
Q1 comp sales expected below the midpoint of full year guide due to severe winter storm activity.
key_opportunities: Pro business growth driven by expanded salesforce, Pro Extended Aisle, and new AI-enabled Pro Companion.
Online sales growth of 10.5% in Q4, with record Black Friday/Cyber Monday.
Acquisitions of FBM and ADG expected to be accretive to adjusted EPS and provide cross-selling opportunities.
Structural demand drivers: record home equity, aging homes (average 44 years), and need for 16 million new homes over next decade.
Lowe's Media Network growth contributing to productivity.

management_tone.label: cautious
management_tone.justification: Management repeatedly uses phrases like 'outlook for 2026 remains cautious given the persistent volatility in housing macro' and 'we are cautiously optimistic just because there's lots of uncertainty out there.'
